survey.architecture: Requests is an HTTP client library for Python that provides a human-friendly interface for making HTTP requests. The library is structured around a request/response abstraction: users construct requests through convenience functions or by using the Session class, which manages connection pooling and settings; requests are then prepared and sent via adapter objects that handle the actual network communication. The core design separates concerns into request construction (Request/PreparedRequest), request sending (Session/HTTPAdapter), and response handling (Response), with supporting systems for authentication, cookies, proxies, timeouts, redirects, and hooks.

conventions: Request vs PreparedRequest distinction: Request is user-facing and mutable; PreparedRequest is immutable and ready for transmission. Users interact with Request; library internals use PreparedRequest.
Session as state container: A Session persists cookies, connection pools, headers, auth, and proxies across multiple requests. It's the recommended way to make multiple requests efficiently.
Adapter pattern for transport: Different URL schemes are handled by different adapters mounted on the Session. HTTPAdapter handles http/https; custom adapters can be registered.
Hook-based extensibility: Response hooks allow post-processing of responses without modifying core code; registered as callables in hooks dict.
Lazy response content: By default, response content is not immediately downloaded (stream=False downloads eagerly, stream=True defers to iter_content()). This is controlled at the Response level.
Proxy and auth merging: Session defaults are merged with per-request overrides; environment variables are consulted if trust_env=True.
Redirect handling: Automatic redirect following (allow_redirects=True) stores intermediate responses in Response.history.
Error translation: urllib3 exceptions are caught and re-raised as requests exceptions (RequestException subclasses) that carry request/response context for debugging.

survey.architecture: Requests is a human-friendly HTTP library for Python that provides a high-level interface for making HTTP requests. It follows a layered architecture: the top level exposes convenient API functions (get, post, etc.) that delegate to a Session object, which manages cookies, connection pooling, and configuration. The Session class coordinates the request-response cycle by preparing Request objects into PreparedRequest objects, dispatching them through pluggable transport adapters (HTTPAdapter), handling redirects, and managing cookies. The adapters translate prepared requests into lower-level urllib3 calls and convert HTTP responses back into Response objects. The system is built around three core abstractions: Request/PreparedRequest for representing outgoing HTTP messages, Response for representing incoming HTTP messages, and adapters for abstracting transport mechanisms.

conventions: Request objects (in models.py) are created by users to specify desired HTTP requests; PreparedRequest objects contain serialized, transmission-ready request data prepared from Request objects merged with Session settings.
The Session class uses adapters as a strategy pattern to handle different URL schemes (http:// vs https://); HTTPAdapter is the default for both, but custom adapters can be registered via mount().
Hook system is response-only and implemented as a dictionary mapping event names to lists of callables; hooks are applied in prepare_request() and dispatched in Session.send() via dispatch_hook().
Cookies are managed at the Session level via RequestsCookieJar and persisted across requests; cookies from responses are extracted and merged for subsequent requests.
Redirect handling is implemented as a generator (resolve_redirects) that yields responses as they're received, updating the initial request's method and auth as needed for each redirect.
Authentication is pluggable via callable AuthBase objects that modify PreparedRequest in prepare_auth(); built-in implementations include HTTPBasicAuth and HTTPDigestAuth.
SSL/TLS verification uses verify parameter: True (default, check certificates), False (skip verification), or a string path to a CA bundle.
Proxies are resolved from environment variables when trust_env=True, or specified explicitly; proxy selection is per-request in Session.send() via select_proxy().

A test server is included in tests/testserver/ for integration testing against a real HTTP endpoint. Tests use pytest and conftest.py for fixtures.
